question.text: Affirmative and veto rights in a Shareholders' Agreement (SHA) typically require:

answer.text: Affirmative vote or express consent of the AIF investor before certain specified corporate actions can be taken by the company, irrespective of shareholding

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, certain specified corporate actions require the affirmative vote or express consent of the AIF investor regardless of shareholding. Examples listed in the workbook include changes to capital structure, alteration of the memorandum/articles, debt above prescribed limits, new fund raising, IPO/listing proposals, business plan changes, subsidiaries/divestments, mergers/reconstitution, asset disposition, winding up, board changes, auditors, and key managerial personnel. The Trap: Affirmative and veto rights are protective rights, not a grant of day-to-day management authority over the company. Note: The breadth of the affirmative/veto list in an SHA is one indicator of the level of investor protection negotiated by the AIF.
